_note: Sources for Form 2 Chemistry (Batches C2-1, C2-2 and C2-3, Terms 1–3). Computed answers follow the rules and tables named here.

atomic-structure.ref: Dalton's atomic theory (1803-1808); protons, neutrons and electrons; Bohr's model with shells of 2, 8, 8 for the first 20 elements; atomic number, mass number, isotopes
atomic-structure.supports: The statements of Dalton's theory and its later corrections; particle charges and masses; electron arrangements; neutrons = mass number − atomic number. Mass numbers used: the most common isotope of each of the first 20 elements (Cl 35).
atomic-structure.checked: Standard results; arrangements and particle numbers computed by code (science2.js, tested). The mass-number table is authored: please check it.

symbols-valency.ref: Chemical symbols (IUPAC), valencies of common elements and radicals, writing formulae by swapping valencies, naming binary compounds (-ide) and compounds with radicals
symbols-valency.supports: Symbols including those from Latin; radicals OH, NO₃, HCO₃, SO₄, CO₃, PO₄, NH₄ with their valencies; formulae and names built from the valency table.
symbols-valency.checked: Formulae and names computed by code from the authored valency table (science2.js): please check the table (copper given valency 2).

periodic-table.ref: History of the periodic table (Döbereiner 1829, Newlands 1864, Mendeleev 1869, Moseley 1913); groups and periods; the families alkali metals, alkaline earth metals, halogens, noble gases; trends in reactivity
periodic-table.supports: Group = outer electrons, period = shells; family names and properties; alkali metals more reactive down the group, halogens less reactive; halogen displacement.
periodic-table.checked: Standard results, dates from general knowledge (not opened in this session): please check them.

reactions-equations.ref: Physical and chemical changes; types of reaction (combination, decomposition, combustion, displacement, neutralisation); word and symbolic equations, state symbols; balancing by coefficients; the law of conservation of mass (Lavoisier) and the closed-flask experiment (lead nitrate + potassium iodide)
reactions-equations.supports: Twenty balanced equations (science2.js, EQ table) with their word forms; atom counts per side; missing masses by addition or subtraction.
reactions-equations.checked: Every equation in the table is checked by atom counting in the tests (eqBalanced). The table of equations and their word forms is authored: please check it, especially the names iron(III) oxide, copper(II) oxide and iron(II) sulphide.

air.ref: Composition of dry air by volume (N₂ 78%, O₂ 21%, Ar about 0.9%, CO₂ about 0.04%); the heated-copper gas-syringe experiment; uses of oxygen, nitrogen, argon and carbon dioxide; air as a mixture; fractional distillation of liquid air
air.supports: Oxygen used = start volume − end volume; percentage = used ÷ start × 100. Boiling points used: N₂ −196 °C, Ar −186 °C, O₂ −183 °C; air liquefied at about −200 °C.
air.checked: Standard values from general knowledge (not opened in this session): please check them.

burning-rusting.ref: Combustion and the fire triangle; complete and incomplete burning (carbon monoxide); burning of paper, cooking gas, wood and cloth; burning of metals and non-metals, basic and acidic oxides; rusting (conditions, the three-tube experiment, Fe₂O₃·xH₂O) and its prevention (painting, oiling, galvanising, tin and chromium plating, sacrificial protection)
burning-rusting.supports: Oxide type from metal/non-metal (science2.js oxideType, using kindOf); aluminium and zinc are left out as amphoteric. Flame colours: Mg white, Na yellow, Ca brick-red, S blue.
burning-rusting.checked: Standard results from general knowledge: please check them, and the safety advice (stop, drop and roll).

separation-purity.ref: States of matter and changes of state; separation by picking, sieving, decanting, filtration, evaporation, crystallisation, magnet, separating funnel, winnowing, simple and fractional distillation, paper and column chromatography, sublimation; melting and boiling points; criteria for purity
separation-purity.supports: State from melting and boiling points (science2.js stateAt); Rf = spot distance ÷ solvent distance (rf). Melting/boiling points used: water 0/100, ethanol −114/78, mercury −39/357, naphthalene 80/218, oxygen −218/−183, sulphur 115/445 °C; methanol boils at 65 °C, propanone at 56 °C.
separation-purity.checked: The table of melting and boiling points is authored from general knowledge: please check it.

fuels.ref: Fossil fuels (coal, crude oil, natural gas): formation, non-renewable; fractions of crude oil and their uses; SONARA (Limbe) and the Kribi gas power station
fuels.checked: General knowledge: please check the Cameroonian examples.

heat-action.ref: Action of heat: hydrates (CuSO₄·5H₂O ⇌ CuSO₄ + 5H₂O), oxides (2HgO → 2Hg + O₂; ZnO yellow when hot), carbonates (→ oxide + CO₂; Na and K carbonates stable), nitrates (Na, K → nitrite + O₂; others → oxide + NO₂ + O₂); mass change of CaCO₃ (44% loss); reversible reactions; tests for CO₂, O₂ and water
heat-action.supports: Equations 20–27 added to the EQ table in science2.js and checked by atom counting.

electrolysis.ref: Conductors and insulators; ionic compounds conduct when molten or dissolved; electrolysis (cathode negative, anode positive); CuCl₂(aq) → Cu + Cl₂; acidified water → 2 H₂ : 1 O₂; molten NaCl → Na + Cl₂; strong and weak electrolytes, non-electrolytes; ORS
electrolysis.supports: Equations 28–30 in science2.js (molten NaCl used instead of PbBr₂ because bromine is not in the element table).
